data.narrative:
Asylon Robotics is a Series B-stage drone and autonomous systems company that has raised $40M to date. The valuation universe consists of eight private peers in the Drones & Autonomous sector, including Elroy Air, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and Archer Aviation. No public comparables exist in this narrow segment.

Given the limited peer set, a traditional peer-median approach is not feasible—only one same-stage comparable was identified, falling short of the minimum three datapoints needed for reliable triangulation. Accordingly, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $40M total capital raised as a proxy baseline. This method implies a valuation of $76M. Sensitivity analysis around this multiplier generates a low estimate of $65M and a high estimate of $87M, reflecting reasonable variance in step-up assumptions across frontier-tech financings.

The median valuation of $76M is supported by a single methodological approach, introducing meaningful uncertainty. The primary risks to this range are stage-specific execution metrics not visible in public filings—particularly unit economics, path to revenue, and technical de-risking in autonomous systems development. A more robust triangulation would require access to adjacent-stage or higher-confidence peer financings in the same subsector. This valuation should be revisited upon material operational or fundraising milestones.
